notes.2.4: Nebkheperure is Tutankhamun. Line 6: tgꜣ is marked doubtful by the editor and is unexplained. Line 7: m snw, 'as an offering (loaf)', is uncertain. Line 8: ꜥft,t is unexplained, perhaps a chest or shrine. Lines 13-15 are broken and their sense is uncertain; in line 15 the deleted signs after hꜣ[ꜣ] are not translated.

nodes.text: That is how the flame came into being in the sky.
As for any excellent scribe who knows the god's words and his utterances, he goes up and he goes down within the sky.
Those of the West cannot drive him away ... (tgꜣ) of the water of his mouth.
His head cannot be taken away as an offering(?).
He does not bow his arms to the tribunal; he enters before the akh-spirits, together with knowing the sayings in the *ꜥft.t*.
No wrong that he did on earth can be reckoned.
Moreover, his gateways are not blocked.
No pestilence can be set against him.
Moreover, you shall say to every great one and to every akh-spirit: It is he who makes plans for the one who has no bread.
His headcloth is not uncovered [...] his clothing [for the great] ones; they see him as divine images in [...] [...]
[...] [...] one [...] who knows(?), enduring in it.
Nothing that is done is done against him, nor is [he] caused to go down [...]
Come, then, my(?) son of the body, beloved, Lord of the Two Lands Nebkheperure.
You shall be with your father Ra as one of these gods who are in his following beside Mehet-weret.
The names of all the gods with whom the Osiris King, Lord of the Two Lands Nebkheperure, will be forever and ever.
They guide [him] on the road of life.
They give him breath, cool water and offerings every day [...]
